summary: Default-deny rules enforce verified-email role boundaries, restrict self-activation to verified Aizu University identities, bind chat sender names to trusted profiles, protect check-in attempts as server-only data, and validate writable schemas. The remaining findings are defense-in-depth improvements rather than direct privilege-escalation paths.

findings.issue: Attachment URLs are length-checked but are not constrained to the project's Firebase Storage origin or the sender's room-scoped object path.
findings.recommendation: Create attachment messages through a callable function, or validate a server-issued Storage object identifier instead of accepting an arbitrary HTTPS URL.

findings.issue: Any signed-in account can create a report, including an unverified or inactive account.
findings.recommendation: Require an active verified role if anonymous-style reporting is not an intentional product requirement.
